collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A coconut crab the size of a small dog sits atop a palm behind the huts: catch it for supper, or let it go about its business.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A coconut crab the size of a small dog has climbed one of the palms behind the huts and is sitting at the top, cracking a coconut with its claws. (friend) is terrified and thrilled at once. (subject) knows two things about coconut crabs: they're delicious, and the old fishers say they take a very, very long time to grow that big.

choices.label: Let It Go About Its Business

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) waits until it climbs down, then catches it carefully with a net and a lot of shouting. The catch is prepared for supper and shared around. (friend) eats some and is very brave about it. Later, (subject) sees (friend.him/her) looking up at the empty palm. "It was really old, wasn't it?" (friend) says. "It was," says (subject). Both things are true: it was very good, and it was very old.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) decides a crab that has lived that long can keep living. They watch it climb down, slowly, carefully, and wander off into the bushes with half a coconut. (friend) names it Grandfather. For the rest of the year, sightings of Grandfather are reported around the village with great excitement. Grandfather does not care about any of this.
